bug_semantics: Before 0.12.0, c3p0 exposed userOverridesAsString as a writable JavaBean/JNDI Reference property containing HexAsciiSerializedMap[<hex Java serialization stream>]. WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource parsed property resets and initial values with C3P0ImplUtils.parseUserOverridesAsString(), which hex-decoded attacker-controlled bytes and passed them to SerializableUtils.fromByteArray() without an allowlist. A crafted serialized ConnectionPoolDataSource or javax.naming.Reference could therefore trigger gadget deserialization and code execution; the historical mchange-commons-java Reference behavior amplified this with remote factoryClassLocation loading.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable parser and reachable property path first appear across a directly testable preserved-tree boundary at e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4, whose parent 15b53cfce6ed1fb0a46fd6597c2b2e4470e6f8c9 lacks the mechanism. The object is explicitly a 270-file import of c3p0-0.9.1-pre5.src.zip, not the atomic SourceForge CVS revision that authored the flaw. The separate root 7ff5d91ae823c8fb9dcdd3f040d274a94bcf4aa6 is an initial post-migration snapshot, and 36182b4a5fd024703e2a36737b2b73ad7237f1f8 is a later reorganization dominated by renames; neither is a smallest real BIC. The unavailable SourceForge member history prevents decomposition to a true BIC.
ai_marker: unavailable: the smallest real BIC and its commit object are not present in the validated public history. The raw aggregate boundary object e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4 names Steve Waldman as author and committer and has only the SourceForge-import subject with no AI trailer or bot identity, but protocol excludes that import object from BIC attribution.
evidence: The assigned first-party advisory data identifies com.mchange:c3p0 versions < 0.12.0 as vulnerable, 0.12.0 as the first patched version, and e14cbd8166e423e2e9a9d6f08b2add3433492d6e as the patch. It describes the writable userOverridesAsString property, crafted serialized objects and javax.naming.Reference inputs, hex-encoded Java serialization, and the mchange-commons-java amplification.

`git log --all --reverse --format=%H%x09%P%x09%s -SuserOverridesAsString -- .` found the property in the parentless 7ff5d91ae823c8fb9dcdd3f040d274a94bcf4aa6 migration snapshot and in e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4 over parent 15b53cfce6ed1fb0a46fd6597c2b2e4470e6f8c9. `git cat-file commit 7ff5d91ae823c8fb9dcdd3f040d274a94bcf4aa6` says only 'Initial commit after migration to git', so that copied root cannot establish authorship. `git show --summary 36182b4a5fd024703e2a36737b2b73ad7237f1f8` reports the later mill-build reorganization and near-total file renames, so it is also rejected as an origin.

`git show --format=fuller --stat --oneline e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4` reports 'source imported from SourceForge (c3p0-0.9.1-pre5.src.zip)' and 270 changed files (3335 insertions, 1250 deletions). This archive aggregate imports the vulnerable parser and property machinery but is not the smallest changeset that wrote them, and the clone supplies no member SHAs with which to decompose it.

The direct boundary-parent command `git grep -n -E 'HexAsciiSerializedMap|parseUserOverridesAsString|userOverridesAsString' 15b53cfce6ed1fb0a46fd6597c2b2e4470e6f8c9 -- src/classes/com/mchange/v2/c3p0` exited 1 with no matches. The same command at e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4 found HASM_HEADER and parseUserOverridesAsString in C3P0ImplUtils.java, listener and initialization calls in WrapperConnectionPoolDataSource.java, the ComboPooledDataSource setter and Reference property, and the pool-manager parser call. This proves the preserved release boundary, not the unavailable true BIC's immediate-parent absence.

`git rev-parse c3p0-0.9.0.4^{} c3p0-0.9.1-pre5^{}` resolved respectively to 15b53cfce6ed1fb0a46fd6597c2b2e4470e6f8c9 and e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4, confirming absence in 0.9.0.4 and presence in 0.9.1-pre5. `git rev-parse v0.11.2^{} v0.12.0^{}` resolved to 51a8e479802edc516ad1b018f6f9c9bf4ae2c09a and afbb946ea70ee2312c1c5fc53dd60dd218f87ef9. The fix is not an ancestor of v0.11.2 (merge-base exit 1) and is an ancestor of v0.12.0 (exit 0), matching the advisory boundary.

`git grep` at v0.11.2 finds the active `SerializableUtils.fromByteArray(serBytes)` sink in C3P0ImplUtils.java. `git show --patch e14cbd8166e423e2e9a9d6f08b2add3433492d6e -- src/com/mchange/v2/c3p0/impl/C3P0ImplUtils.java` shows that this one-file commit comments out the serialization implementation and installs the active FastCsvUtils ragged-CSV create/parse methods. It therefore directly removes the attacker-controlled ObjectInputStream path and is both fix_sha and direct_fix_sha.

The marker_state disagreement is resolved by `git cat-file commit e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4`: the raw object has tree c9ce06a9cbefa70f8e1e9c5c0ea733cf292fb8a6, parent 15b53cfce6ed1fb0a46fd6597c2b2e4470e6f8c9, author and committer Steve Waldman <swaldman@mchange.com>, and only the SourceForge-import subject. There is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot marker. The primary's `unavailable` marker state wins because this object is an excluded archive aggregate rather than the BIC; the reviewer's no-marker observation about the boundary object is factually correct ancillary evidence but cannot support an `absent` BIC marker state. The later 415662b4e75bc3b8f7408b7fc47b9e77c1946584 subject 'Claude-generated tests of deserialization-gadget mitigations' is later test work and is rejected as non-BIC evidence.
reasoning: The causal flaw is reachable unrestricted Java deserialization of the externally settable userOverridesAsString value. The preserved history proves that the full mechanism is absent in the 0.9.0.4 snapshot and present in the 0.9.1-pre5 snapshot, while the advisory-linked patch directly replaces the active format/parser and lands before v0.12.0 but not v0.11.2. Those checks close the vulnerability, direct-fix, and release-boundary gates. They do not close the introducer gate: e11fd1340644747977fa34bc3377704223b6ccb4 is explicitly a 270-file release-ZIP import, 7ff5d91ae823c8fb9dcdd3f040d274a94bcf4aa6 is a parentless migration snapshot, and 36182b4a5fd024703e2a36737b2b73ad7237f1f8 is a later move/reorganization. None is the smallest changeset that authored the vulnerable lines. For the sole assigned marker_state disagreement, the protocol permits AI attribution only from the smallest real BIC commit object. Since that object is unavailable, the canonical state is `unavailable`, as the primary claimed. The reviewer correctly found no AI marker on the boundary import object, but treating that as BIC-level `absent` evidence would violate the aggregate-import and BIC-only rules. With no verified smallest BIC or direct-parent check for it, BLOCKED is the gate-complete verdict despite the verified fix.
remaining_gap: Recover the original SourceForge CVS revision or revisions underlying c3p0-0.9.1-pre5, identify the smallest atomic revision that first wrote the unsafe HexAsciiSerializedMap parser and reachable writable/listener/Reference path, verify that revision's immediate parent lacks the mechanism, and inspect that original revision's commit object for AI identity or trailers. Until that member history is available, introducer_sha, introducer_parent, true-parent absence, decomposition, and BIC marker state cannot be closed beyond `unavailable`.
